member_targets: The physical mechanism by which temperature变化 alters an instrument's pitch — i.e., how thermal changes affect the properties (e.g., air column speed of sound, string tension/length, material dimensions) that determine sounding frequency.

The physical/acoustic mechanism by which temperature changes and instrument behavior alter an instrument's sounding pitch after initial tuning, causing drift from the shared reference.
The physical mechanism by which temperature changes alter an instrument's sounding pitch (e.g., effects on air column speed of sound, material expansion, string tension) during performance.
The mechanism and direction by which temperature change alters an instrument's pitch/intonation over the course of a performance.
The mechanism by which temperature changes and instrument behavior alter an instrument's pitch/intonation over the course of a performance, and the direction of those effects.

The mechanism by which temperature changes and instrument behavior alter an instrument's pitch/intonation during performance, and the direction and nature of those effects on players' intonation choices.

The perceptual or judgmental criteria ensemble players use to determine that an intonation adjustment has achieved sufficient alignment — i.e., what cues or standards signal 'in tune enough' during tuning and performance.
